newsitem.title: USA: Dekalb says resistant corn patent intact.
newsitem.headline: Dekalb says resistant corn patent intact.

text.p: Dekalb Genetics Corp said its patent on a type of corn resistant to certain herbicides remains intact, despite a federal court ruling on it.
The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois granted a stay to AgrEvo USA Co in a patent infringement lawsuit initiated by Dekalb, the company said.
The ruling temporarily suspends Dekalb's legal proceeding to enforce its patent rights against AgrEvo, Dekalb said.
"This ruling does not change anything regarding our patent and legal position," said chief executive Bruce Bickner.

"The court's ruling does not address the validity or enforceability of Dekalb's product patent position regarding corn that is resistant to glufosinate herbicides, such as AgrEvo's Liberty herbicide. In fact, Dekalb's patent rights with respect to glufosinate resistant corn remain fully intact as issued on August 27, 1996," said the seed company.
AgrEvo, a unit of a joint venture between Hoechst AG and Schering AG, has asked the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to declare an interference proceeding with regard to the Dekalb patent.
"The court decided to suspend the court proceedings temporarily to give the patent office time to decide whether to declare an interference," Dekalb said.
